content.text: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on IBM exists anywhere in the document; the only restrictive covenants run against MSL, and the CDA expressly preserves freedom to compete.

input.quote: 1) providing to others products or services which may be competitive with products or services of the Discloser; 2) providing products or services to others who compete with the Discloser; or 3) assigning its employees in any way it may choose.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on IBM. Searches for competing-product, exclusivity, sole-source, requirements-purchase and field-of-use/territory language return nothing binding IBM. The only restrictive covenant, § 14.18 (Restrictions and Limitations), runs against MSL (limiting MSL's use of IBM property and requiring MSL to protect IBM delivery schedules), which benefits us and is not flagged. The change-of-control trigger at § 5.1(v) ("substantially all of the shares or assets of one Party are acquired by an entity that competes directly with the other Party") is a mutual termination trigger, not a covenant restricting the businesses IBM may operate or the products it may buy or build. Affirmatively, the CDA confirms that receipt of Information "will not preclude, or in any way limit, the Recipient from" providing competitive products or services or serving the Discloser's competitors. This meets the preferred position, so no redline is proposed.
